# Typography and invisible characters

French orthography puts a no-break space before a colon : like this. Numbers such as 10 000 use a narrow no-break space. Both are a single space on screen and must normalize to one, or a quote copied from the page will never be found.

Some documents carry a zerowidth space inside a word. Others carry a softhyphen. Neither is visible, so neither belongs in the stored body. A family emoji 👨👩👧 is different: the joiners are part of the character.

Emphasis such as this phrase and that phrase is formatting, not text. The stored body keeps the words and drops the markers. Links that still resolve but no longer say the same thing are the dangerous case.

Combining marks appear in words like café and naïve. The stored form is composed, because that is what a browser hands you when you copy from the screen.
